title: Converge legacy version-gateway semantics and harmonize flag TTLs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Remove and unify multiple overlapping versioning semantics used by our routing and admin surfaces and standardize flag TTL/expiry behavior across hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
Background: Over the years we accumulated three separate version gating mechanisms (vparam query shims, route manifest fingerprints, and a legacy version gateway service) plus several code paths that encode flag lifetime differently. This causes inconsistent rollout behavior, occasional stale flag reads in Dedicated clusters, and confusion for SREs and support engineers.
Scope: - Decommission the legacy version-gateway service and replace its runtime routing by manifest-based routing with strict fingerprint validation.
- Migrate all flag lifetime (TTL/expiry) metadata to a single canonical field (flag_ttl_seconds) and retire the older "expires_at" and TTL-override shims.
- Add migration tooling to backfill canonical field and a compatibility layer for 30 days to avoid breaking older clients.
- Update admin APIs and console surfaces to show canonical TTL and a migration status banner.
Success metrics: - Zero customer-facing errors after compat window for all canary customers.
- Reduce variance in rollout timing across clusters to < 2% for canary cohorts.
- Remove 4K LOC of routing compatibility code.
Rollout plan: 1) Feature branch: introduce canonical field, migration scripts, and schema validators. 2) Internal canary: runtime-1.22 in staging with manual canary for 5 internal teams. 3) Gradual migration: backfill flags over a 24-hour window per region; enable strict manifest validation behind a runtime flag. 4) Open compatibility window (30 days) with monitoring for stale reads and error spikes. 5) Final cutover: remove gateway and shims, ship cleanup patch.
Monitoring & KPIs: dashboards for flag read latency, stale-read rate, manifest mismatch counts, and rollback counts. Observability hooks added in migration script to emit events to tracing and metrics.
Migration artifacts & refs: - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Version+Gateway+Convergence - Migration script (staging): https://git.internal.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/-/blob/feat/flag-ttl-migration/scripts/backfill_ttl.py - Design note for console changes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aB2C-design-note - Risk assessment: highest risk is accidental strict validation that rejects legitimate older manifests. Mitigation: opt-in strict mode and conservative canary sizing. Rollback plan: re-enable gateway compatibility proxy, revert strict validation flag, and stop backfill job. Security review rationale: flag fields can influence routing decisions and may surface in audit logs; a security review is required before final cutover.
acceptance_criteria: All existing flags have canonical flag_ttl_seconds populated or an explicit migration-state tag
No production traffic is routed to the legacy version-gateway after opt-in canary completes
Console shows canonical TTL and migration banner for at least 30 days
Automated tests cover canonical field parsing for hosted/dedicated/private code paths
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Console, and SRE. Decision: 30-day compatibility window and phased backfill per region.
2025-01-20: Prototype backfill script implemented; initial small-scale backfill in staging completed. Observed ~0.8% transient increase in admin API latency — SRE to monitor.
2025-01-28: RFC posted outlining strict-manifest validation semantics. PM and Security left comments; security requested additional audit events and retention note.
2025-02-02: First internal canary (5 internal teams) started in us-central1. No errors observed after 6 hours; manifest mismatch metric stable.
2025-02-07: PR #4217 opened to add schema validators and console banner; awaiting design review and security checklist items.
notes: Engineering trade-offs: We considered a gradual translation layer that would translate vparam queries to manifest fingerprints at the gateway level but decided it added more moving parts and would prolong maintenance burden. We prioritized a single canonical representation to simplify future rollout tooling. Follow-ups: - ENG-341900: create a lint rule that enforces canonical flag field on new flag writes. - PM to schedule customer comms for Dedicated customers before final cutover.
